data.text:
The five-second epistemology of the cloth mask progression, Asia edition.
Japan allowing more coal-fired power. The less efficient plants. The ones that were restricted from capacity auctions to tackle climate change. Climate change just got tackled by the Strait. The architecture’s war producing the energy crisis that produces the coal that produces the emissions the architecture’s climate agreements were supposed to prevent. The architecture destroying its own climate agenda with its own war. Add it to the list.

The Philippines declared a national energy emergency and bought Russian crude. Bangladesh closed universities to save electricity. Sri Lanka reintroduced weekly fuel rationing. India is facing a cooking gas shortage. Japan won’t share reserves and is firing up coal plants that were supposed to be retired. The cloth mask progression going global. Every country reaching for the dirtiest thing on the shelf because the clean thing transited the Strait the architecture closed.

Japan imports 93% of its oil through Hormuz. 93%. The architecture’s Pacific ally more dependent on the Strait than anyone except the Romanovs. Japan released 80 million barrels from reserves. 45 days of demand. The reserves buying time the way the SPR buys time the way the jawboning buys time. The time running out at the rate the coal plants fire up. Every country’s progression is the same — reserves first, then rationing, then coal, then whatever’s left. The E15 was the social distancing. The Sable pipe was the cloth mask. The CARBOB waiver was the vaccine. The coal plant is the lockdown. Japan just entered lockdown.

Ghalibaf da Gangsta asked if they can print gas molecules. Can they print LNG from a Qatar that declared force majeure. Can they print clean energy from a Strait that’s closed. Can they print climate targets from coal plants. The architecture’s war just set the climate agenda back a decade to keep the lights on for a month. Some coal. Some climate. Some 93%. Some Strait. Day 28.

profile_bio.description: The Strait at zero. The dashboard vs. the war. The five-second epistemology vs. the ground truth.
